subject: engine.advancePhase() is called by 71 boxes and BoxEngine has no such member
description:
Found by the new derived-allowlist BOX-003 (task 384) within a minute of it existing -- the denylist could never have found it. BoxEngine defines _advancePhase() (underscore, line ~3578) which takes NO arguments and is gated on config.blueTeamMode; the 71 boxes call engine.advancePhase('recon') WITH a phase-name argument. Different name, different signature. NOT a crash: every call site is guarded as `engine.advancePhase && engine.advancePhase('x')`, so it is a silent no-op. Normal phase progression appears to run through _checkPhaseProgression(flagId), which IS called internally (BoxEngine.js:258, 1828, 1854), so students are probably unaffected -- but that is a hypothesis, NOT verified, and 'probably fine' is what was said about resetLab. NEEDS: (a) confirm in a browser that phases actually advance in one of the 71 boxes, (b) decide whether the intended call was _advancePhase (then the boxes are wrong and blueTeamMode boxes may be broken) or whether a public advancePhase(name) was meant to exist (then the engine is missing it), (c) note _advancePhase itself has ZERO callers anywhere -- it is dead engine code either way. Other unknowns from the same sweep, 1 box each: addCommand, removeCommand, unlockPhase, browser, resolvePath, getFile, log, padEnd -- triage separately, some are likely filesystem strings not calls. All 79 are BASELINED so they do not block deploys; they are visible in _tools/reports/BOX_ENGINE_API_BASELINE.json.
[2026-09-13 21:34] SHIPPED + VERIFIED LIVE 2026-09-13 (53e278806). Answer: NEITHER reading was right. _advancePhase() is blueTeamMode-only and takes no args; no box sets blueTeamMode, so even the correctly-spelled call did nothing. Removed all 437 statements from 71 boxes; deliberately did NOT add a public advancePhase(id), which would complete phases without their requiredFlags. Phases were never broken -- verified on production before and after: activeAtBoot ['recon'], tracker renders, phases complete and unlock. NANCY BLOCKED IT and found a regression I introduced: in e9-ghost-production the dead call was the sole body of a compound if, so removal left the if header capturing the next statement and made a student-visible return conditional (node --check passed; my leftover-reference check counted the one thing the bug did not leave). Fixed, and verification REPLACED not patched: strip every advancePhase line from pre-removal and current text, require byte-identity -- 71 checked, 0 differing, three independent derivations agreeing (mine, Nancy's, Chris's). BOX-003 findings 79 -> 8. e9 cat path confirmed on production from a cold box.
